title: harbor-master-receives-a-watch
intention: harbor_master receives a WATCHME's finding: a bus verb 'watch' takes {ticket, holds, finding} from a probe, and a finding that the ticket's falsifier no longer holds sends that ticket back to FIXME with the finding as its lack.
why: Every standing probe mails harbor_master or a peer and nothing reads it (835b5736bf2b D2): a WATCHME red that lives only in an unread mailbox is an error collapsed to silence (Law 7). Akien's answer to open-291189a9766a: build the receivers.
traces_to: Akien's answer to open-291189a9766a (WATCHME = probe + receiver: 'for all watchmes that we built probes for but not recievers, i think we just build the recievers'), the 2026-09-30 ruling that a probe's data must have a consumer that USES it, and Law 7 (a red that lives only in a mailbox nobody reads is an error collapsed to silence)
how: Add 'watch' to HarborMasterDevice.declared_verbs (cairn/devices/cairn/machines/harbor_master/device.py). The handler reads body {ticket, holds, finding} and refuses as data (accepted False, reason) when the ticket is missing or does not resolve, when holds is not a bool, or when holds is False with an empty finding. holds True returns accepted True with acted 'none' and changes nothing. holds False resolves the ticket's live workflow_and_state and owning component, then calls the existing clearance._send_to_fixme(workflow, ticket, [{kind: 'watchme', why: finding}], actor=<envelope sender>, history_path, state_path). That is the same back-edge a refused PROVED crossing takes, written through the artifact door. It replies with that function's sentence. A ticket already at FIXME or in a terminal state is not moved, and the reply says so. Proof: a fixture world with a PROVED code-seam ticket; post a watch with holds False and assert the cursor reads [FIXME:waiting] and the fixme list holds the finding; post holds True and assert nothing changes; post malformed bodies and assert each is refused by name. History: the crossing journals at the component holding the ticket's probe (walk up from watchme.probe to the first intention+why.json). _send_to_fixme gains a keyword why.
falsifier: Falsifier stated: GREEN when posting watch {ticket: T, holds: false, finding: F} to harbor_master over a fixture world (clearance._crossing_roots patched, the test_clearance.py:1564 pattern) with T a PROVED code-seam ticket leaves T at [FIXME:waiting], its fixme list carrying F, and one journaled crossing in the history.json of the component that holds T's probe; holds true leaves T's bytes unchanged; each malformed body (no ticket, unresolvable ticket, holds not a bool, holds false with empty finding) is refused by name with nothing written; a ticket not at a rest (PROVED or WATCHME) is not moved and the reply says so. RED if a holds:false finding leaves T where it was, holds:true writes anything, or the handler touches the live corpus from a fixture world. Horizon: the first per-component child whose probe posts watch.
watchme: none, because the receiver's use is read by the per-component children of 835b5736bf2b (CairnCommons/tickets/835b5736bf2b-every-probe-has-a-receiver.json, decision D2), whose probes post to this verb and whose own WATCHME specs name it as receiver; a probe on the receiver itself would need a receiver of its own.
children: none, because the change is one verb handler in device.py and one keyword on clearance._send_to_fixme.
builder_notes: A Haiku builder would ask: (1) Where? cairn/devices/cairn/machines/harbor_master/device.py: add "watch": self._handle_watch to declared_verbs; _handle_watch(envelope) reads body {ticket, holds, finding}, actor = envelope['sender'] (refuse with no sender, as clear does). (2) Resolution: roots = clearance._crossing_roots(); tickets dir = roots['commons']/tickets or TICKETS_DIR; repo = roots['repo'] or CAIRN_ROOT; glob <tickets>/<id>-*.json must hit exactly one; the ticket's watchme must be a dict with a probe path; walk up from repo/probe's parent to the first dir with intention+why.json; history_path = that/history.json, state_path = that/state.json. (3) Rest test: the cursor token (parse_workflow(w).path[cursor]) must be PROVED or start with WATCHME; else reply acted 'none' with the cursor. (4) Action: clearance._send_to_fixme(w, id, [{'kind':'watchme','why':finding}], actor=actor, history_path=..., state_path=..., why=f'a WATCHME finding: {finding}') and reply {accepted: True, verb:'watch', acted:'fixme'|'none', said: <sentence>}. (5) Proof: new cairn/devices/cairn/machines/harbor_master/proofs/test_watch_receives_a_finding.py, a fixture world under tempfile with commons/tickets/<id>-x.json and repo/<comp>/intention+why.json + probes/p.py, _crossing_roots patched; teeth a_red_finding_sends_the_ticket_to_fixme, a_green_finding_writes_nothing, a_malformed_watch_is_refused_by_name, a_ticket_not_at_rest_is_not_moved.

decisions.text: D1: write the proof first, red — Create cairn/devices/cairn/machines/harbor_master/proofs/test_watch_receives_a_finding.py, copying the fixture-world pattern of cairn/devices/cairn/machines/harbor_master/proofs/test_clearance.py _fixture_journals (line ~1559): build a world under tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='watch-receives-a-finding-'), then patch `clearance._crossing_roots = lambda: {'repo': world, 'commons': world / 'commons', 'instance': world / 'instance'}` and restore it in finally. The world holds: world/commons/tickets/<tid>-fixture-watched.json with {'id': tid, 'title': 'fixture-watched', 'workflow_and_state': 'code-seam@v2: THINKME -> TICKETME -> BUILDME -> PROVEME -> [PROVED]', 'watchme': {'probe': 'comp/probes/p.py'}}; world/comp/intention+why.json containing '{}'; world/comp/probes/p.py containing ''. tid is any 12 hex, e.g. 'ab12cd34ef56'. Drive the device by calling the handler directly: `HarborMasterDevice(...)._handle_watch({'sender': 'fixture_prober', 'body': {...}})` — construct the device as `HarborMasterDevice()` (test_fleet_cache.py:64 does the same). Four teeth, each a function printing PASS/FAIL with its name, exit 1 on any FAIL: a_red_finding_sends_the_ticket_to_fixme (holds False, finding 'fixture finding': reply acted 'fixme'; ticket workflow_and_state contains '[FIXME:waiting]'; ticket fixme == [{'n': 1, 'kind': 'watchme', 'missing': 'fixture finding'}]; world/comp/history.json exists and its last record's 'to' is 'FIXME'); a_green_finding_writes_nothing (holds True on a fresh world: ticket bytes identical before/after, no world/comp/history.json, reply acted 'none'); a_malformed_watch_is_refused_by_name (each of: body without ticket; ticket 'ffffffffffff' that does not resolve; holds 'yes'; holds False with finding ''; a ticket whose watchme has no probe; an envelope with no sender — reply accepted False and its reason names the field ('ticket', 'ticket', 'holds', 'finding', 'probe', 'sender'), ticket bytes unchanged); a_ticket_not_at_rest_is_not_moved (a ticket at 'code-seam@v2: THINKME -> TICKETME -> [BUILDME] -> PROVEME -> PROVED' with holds False: reply acted 'none', reason names the cursor, bytes unchanged). Add the PROVES header the other harbor proofs carry, naming a88d6a368cfb and the four teeth. Run it before D2/D3: it must exit 1.

D2: the why keyword on _send_to_fixme — In cairn/devices/cairn/machines/harbor_master/clearance.py, _send_to_fixme gains a keyword-only `why: str | None = None`. When None it keeps today's text exactly: emit's why stays f'clearance refused at PROVED: {len(lacks)} lack(s)' and the ticket write's why stays f'{boat_id}: clearance refused at PROVED — sent to FIXME with {len(lacks)} missing'. When given, both use it: emit(why=why) and the write why=f'{boat_id}: {why}'. Nothing else in the function changes. Then run cairn/devices/cairn/machines/harbor_master/proofs/test_clearance.py; it must stay green.

D3: the watch verb — In cairn/devices/cairn/machines/harbor_master/device.py, declared_verbs gains `"watch": self._handle_watch` beside 'clear'. _handle_watch(self, envelope) -> dict, every reply carrying verb 'watch' and device self.device_id. Refusals, in this order, each `accepted: False` with a reason naming the field: no envelope sender ('sender'); body ticket missing or not a str ('ticket'); holds not a bool ('holds'); holds False and finding not a non-empty str ('finding'); the ticket file does not resolve to exactly one under <tickets>/<id>-*.json or <id>.json ('ticket'); the ticket's watchme is not a dict with a non-empty str 'probe' ('probe'); walking up from <repo>/<probe>'s parent finds no directory holding intention+why.json before <repo> ('probe'). Here roots = clearance._crossing_roots(); tickets = Path(roots['commons'])/'tickets' if roots else Path(clearance.TICKETS_DIR); repo = Path(roots['repo']) if roots else Path(clearance.CAIRN_ROOT). holds True: reply {accepted: True, acted: 'none', said: 'the falsifier holds; nothing changes'} and write nothing. holds False: wf = parse_workflow(doc['workflow_and_state']) from cairn.tools.base.transitions; token = wf.here; when token not in ('PROVED', 'WATCHME') reply {accepted: True, acted: 'none', said: f'the ticket stands at {token}, not at a rest; a WATCHME finding moves only a PROVED or WATCHME ticket'}. Otherwise said = clearance._send_to_fixme(doc['workflow_and_state'], tid, [{'kind': 'watchme', 'why': finding}], actor=sender, history_path=str(comp/'history.json'), state_path=str(comp/'state.json'), why=f'a WATCHME finding: {finding}'); re-read the ticket; acted = 'fixme' when its workflow_and_state changed, else 'none' (a class with no FIXME: _send_to_fixme's sentence says why); reply {accepted: True, acted, said}. Docstring: the receiver of 835b5736bf2b D2, Akien's answer to open-291189a9766a, actor-is-sender as in _handle_clear.

D4: green, then commit — Run cairn/devices/cairn/machines/harbor_master/proofs/test_watch_receives_a_finding.py (exit 0) and cairn/devices/cairn/machines/harbor_master/proofs/test_clearance.py (exit 0). Commit device.py, clearance.py and the proof with message 'a88d6a368cfb: harbor_master receives a watch' in the background (the commit runs the reseal ladder).
